items: NullPointerException is a common cause of application failures.
The if construct is widely used for null checks, but it intertwines null checks with business logic, which can clutter the code.
Java 8 introduces the Optional class to decouple null checks from business logic and improve code readability.
The Optional class, found in the java.util package, is a container object which may or may not hold a non-null value.
It offers methods to handle null checks more efficiently, keeping code clean and concise.
Example: Using Optional in a class with a passport for a FullTimeEmployee.
Optional<T> empty(): Returns an empty Optional (i.e., no value).
T get(): Returns the value if present; otherwise, throws NoSuchElementException.
boolean isPresent(): Returns true if a value is present, otherwise returns false.
T orElse(T other): Returns the value if present, otherwise returns the provided argument (default value).
Optional<T> of(T value): Returns an Optional containing the given non-null value.
Optional<T> ofNullable(T value): Returns an Optional containing the value if non-null, otherwise returns an empty Optional.

Optional<U> flatMap(Function<? super T, Optional<U>> mapper): Applies the specified mapping function if the value is present and returns the result as an Optional. If absent, returns an empty Optional.
Optional<U> map(Function<? super T, ? extends U> mapper): Applies the specified mapping function to the value if present, and if the result is non-null, returns an Optional wrapping the result.
Task: Retrieve passport numbers of full-time employees, defaulting to 0 if not available.
flatMap(): Used for methods that return an Optional. Here, FullTimeEmployee.getPassport() returns an Optional<Passport>, so we use flatMap() to handle it.
map(): Used for methods that return a non-Optional value. Here, Passport.getPassportNo() returns an int, so we use map() to extract the passport number and wrap it in an Optional.
orElse(0): Provides a default value (0) if the passport is not present.
Reduces NullPointerExceptions: By avoiding manual null checks, Optional helps to prevent null pointer exceptions.
Decouples Business Logic from Null Checks: Keeps the business logic clean by decoupling the handling of potential null values.
Improves Readability: The code becomes more declarative and readable with built-in null handling methods.

content.text: Using Optional in Java 8 helps manage null values in a cleaner, more elegant way by encapsulating them inside an Optional container. This avoids verbose null checks and improves code maintainability.
